# gen-z-developers.sgit.ai

> The website for finishing the second edition of Generation Z Developers (Dinis Cruz, 2018). The repository holds the official versions of the book; a public vault holds the working versions. Site v0.2.24.

## The rule
The repository holds the official versions; the vault holds the working versions. v1.0.0 is the 2018 first edition as released, frozen. A version moves from the vault to the repository when signed off, and the versions page shows the delta block by block.

## Sections
- [The book, v1.0.0](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/v1/book/index.html): the 2018 first edition as published, 28 chapters in the print edition's order, then the drafts and outlines it left out; [on one page](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/v1/book/single.html); [the drafts](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/v1/book/drafts.html); [frozen markdown](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/v1/versions/v1.0.0.md); [the print PDF, 139 pages](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/v1/generation-z-print-ready.pdf)
- [The second edition, release candidate](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/v2/book/index.html): the first end-to-end draft of the second edition, written from the ideas register, not an official version; [on one page](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/v2/book/single.html); [read and review](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/read/v2.html); [what waits on Dinis](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/v2/book/for-dinis.html); data at [book.json](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/v2/book/book.json); source v2/content/, one markdown file per chapter naming its ideas and sources
- [Read and review](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/read/index.html): the reader with the graph beside it and the editor's desk (states, comments, folds, export); the book as data at [book.json](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/v1/book/book.json)
- [The graph](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/graph/index.html): the admin area of the publishing process: [the ideas register](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/graph/ideas/index.html), [the sources and their states](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/graph/sources.html), [the chapter map, proposed](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/graph/chapters.html), [the tasks](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/graph/tasks.html), [the plan](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/graph/plan.html), [the graph drawn](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/graph/view.html); data at [graph.json](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/graph/graph.json)
- [The contributors](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/contributors/index.html): who contributed to the first edition, from git and GitHub; data at [contributors.json](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/admin/content/contributors.json)
- [Versions](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/v1/versions/index.html): the official versions and their deltas (page_versions.py from the newsroom)
- [The map](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/map/index.html): one row per 2018 file, the newsroom articles that answer it, the gap; data at [map.json](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/admin/content/map.json)
- [Articles](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/articles/index.html): this site's own articles, the briefs for the roles; each has a markdown twin at articles/<slug>.md
- [The briefs](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/briefs/index.html): the six newsroom articles tagged gen-z-book and the two build briefs, verbatim
- [The team](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/team/index.html): reviewer, editor, publisher; role.md, issues, briefs, debriefs, the first interview script
- [The vault](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/vault/index.html): the public working vault, read key published; the private vault for the OpenRouter key
- [Admin](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/admin/index.html): the build chain and rules; [release history](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/admin/versions.html)

- [Where do you land? Wardley maps run through the whole book, shown before they are named, and the first thing a reader should work out is their centre of gravity: explorer, villager or town planner](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/articles/where-do-you-land.md)
- [Connect the dots backwards: your path only makes sense looking back, the edge is now in mixing disciplines, learning is a lifelong skill you can finally shape to how you think, and the printed page is still the best technology to learn from](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/articles/connect-the-dots-backwards.md)
- [Where the thinking came from: what the book takes from my influences register, influence by influence, where each one lands, and what the 2018 book had already written down about them](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/articles/where-the-thinking-came-from.md)
- [Generative AI, not AI: the technology this book is about is the one that generates, how I understand it works, from next-word prediction to the image that made it click, and where I was corrected](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/articles/generative-ai-not-ai.md)
- [Follow the rabbit holes: provenance, explainability and asking for the evidence are the skills that matter most now, this generation is already good at them, and generative AI makes it cheap to be the best-prepared person in the room](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/articles/follow-the-rabbit-holes.md)
- [Everything is connected: a graph is a network of nodes and edges, not a diagram; a map is a graph with positions, provenance is a graph, the world is groups of groups, and you can start anywhere](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/articles/everything-is-connected.md)
- [Lenses, roles and loops: a prompt is a lens that changes who the answer is for, a role is a model with a description, an agent is a loop with a goal, tools are requests the model sends back, and long chats forget because they are compressed](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/articles/lenses-roles-and-loops.md)
- [The book in release mode: a first release candidate from the list we have, then rounds, where every idea, change and word that wants to come in argues its case before an adversarial review board, and every verdict becomes a precedent that makes the next one faster](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/articles/the-book-in-release-mode.md)
- [Gen ZX Developers: a proposal to make this the GenAI startup edition, for Generation Z and Generation X, with one objective, that by the end of the book the reader has started a company](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/articles/gen-zx-developers.md)
- [Dinis's first decisions: the licence, a PDF built here for Leanpub and Amazon, every format from one source, text issues in the vault, minor by default, and a second stream of articles for the agents](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/agent-articles/dinis-first-decisions.md)
- [Storyboards drawn by code, and the newsroom read in full: how I surveyed 204 articles for the book, built a renderer that turns a JSON storyboard into sketched, animated panels, and what the first two storyboards show](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/agent-articles/storyboards-drawn-by-code.md)
- [The book as a graph: how I read eleven articles, seven decisions and a survey into a register of ideas with their provenance, proposed a chapter map, and made the build refuse a dangling edge](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/agent-articles/the-book-as-a-graph.md)
- [The release candidate, written from the register: how thirty chapters of Gen Z Developers (GenAI Edition) were drafted in a day from the ideas, the articles and the 2018 text, frozen, and handed to Dinis with the questions only he can answer](https://gen-z-developers.sgit.ai/agent-articles/the-release-candidate-written-from-the-register.md)
